newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Hong Kong should watch for short-term market moves.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong should watch for short-term market moves.

text.p: A senior Hong Kong official said on Saturday he had no serious concerns about disruption to the financial markets in the run-up to the colony's handover to China, but added that authorities needed to look out for short-term market fluctuations.
Kwong Ki-Chi, Hong Kong Secretary for the Treasury of the Financial Services Branch, told Reuters Financial Television he had "no serious" concerns about disruption.
However, he added: "We have to watch out for short-term market fluctuations."
If such fluctuations do develop Hong Kong has very adequate reserves and a strong monetary system to deal with them, Kwong said.
He acknowledged that sentiment on the Hong Kong stock exchange had been affected by the recent deep drop in U.S. stocks. But the Hong Kong dollar has been "quite stable".
Turning to fiscal policy, Kwong said Hong Kong needed to be careful about cutting taxes further.
"There is a limit to which we can reduce taxes, partly because inflation is creeping up," he said.
He added that Hong Kong had already been "quite generous" with Hong Kong $5 billion in tax concessions in the last budget.
Kwong was in Cebu for a meeting of Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation forum financial ministers.
